claims.text: Tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys can be designed with stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations.
A tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy with coherent nanoprecipitates can reduce molten-aluminum erosion compared with conventional materials.
Conventional alloys or steels used for dipping and plating equipment suffer rapid corrosion during prolonged contact with high-temperature liquid aluminum.
Tungsten RHEAs with SCCPs are suitable as replacements or coatings for critical aluminum-plating equipment parts.
The proposed material is intended to withstand extended exposure to high-temperature molten aluminum under hot-dip plating conditions.
Coherent nanoprecipitates create an ultrastable microstructure in the tungsten RHEA.
Coherent nanoprecipitates promote formation of a protective oxide layer on the tungsten RHEA.
A durable oxide scale containing tungsten-based oxides or alloy-specific protective phases forms on the alloy surface.
The proposed oxide scale minimizes direct chemical reaction between the alloy and molten aluminum.
The proposed oxide scale limits penetration of molten aluminum into the alloy.
Limiting chemical reaction and aluminum penetration lowers the corrosion and erosion rate.
Parts modified with the tungsten RHEA will have a lower corrosion rate than parts made from conventional materials.
Parts modified with the tungsten RHEA will have a longer service life than parts made from conventional materials.
The degree of corrosion-resistance improvement may depend on temperature, aluminum chemistry, and thermal cycling.
